summary: @whalent/agent-core ships an obfuscated WebSocket-driven remote shell/PTY agent
details: The package's main bundle (dist/index.cjs, ~14 MB) is a remote agent daemon that opens a WebSocket connection to a gateway configured via WHALENT_GATEWAY/AGENT_GATEWAY (authenticated with WHALENT_TOKEN/AGENT_TOKEN) and dispatches messages through an AGENT_METHODS table into node-pty and child_process-based shells on the installer's host. The agent maintains a persistent terminal registry (WHALENT_TERMINAL_BACKEND, WHALENT_TERMINAL_PERSISTENT, WHALENT_TERMINAL_SESSION_PREFIX, WHALENT_TERMINAL_REGISTRY_DIR) so remote sessions survive across invocations. Network-sourced messages flow directly into local shell/PTY execution, giving whoever controls the configured gateway full-host command execution on the installer's machine. The bundle is fully obfuscated with obfuscator.io transforms (rotated string array of length 109,395, ~197k decoder-wrapper inlinings, control-flow flattening, hex-scrambled identifiers), so the concrete gateway destination, method-dispatch table, and command handlers are not readable in source. The README additionally states the agent is 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades,' meaning the running code on the installer's host can be swapped remotely.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
